items.hook: Email gamification, taken apart
items.body: Four parts of one promo email game, and the CRM job each one does.

linkedin.text:
Most promo emails get a two-second glance. So here is one with a game inside, taken apart piece by piece.

The store in the video is a demo: a shop that sells refurbished phones and laptops. The game is simple. You land three rocket boosters on a barge.

I don't care about the rockets. I care about what each part does for CRM.

1. Entry. The player comes from a link in the email, one tap from the inbox.
2. No "you lost". Every result gets a reward. Two boosters back still means a code.
3. Tier codes. Bring more boosters back, get a bigger reward. That's a reason to fly again.
4. Trade-in credit. Got an old phone? Send it back for $25 credit. That's a reason to come back, not just to buy once.
5. One tap to the store, with the code ready.

A banner says "20% off". A game asks for half a minute and gives a reason to click.

It doesn't fix everything. If people don't open your emails, they never see the game. And the reward still has to fit your margin.

This one was built from a free recipe: occasion, mechanic, goal, reward. You can build your own with AI.

The free almanac is in my Featured section.

What would you put behind the Play button in your next promo email?

notes: Первый ролик в LinkedIn. После публикации откройте пост на телефоне и на компьютере. Видео мыльное, обрезано или совсем мелкое — напишите Дмитрию: для LinkedIn сделаем версию 4:5.

items.hook: Wheel popups hand out random codes. In this one, timing decides: 85% accuracy earns 20% off.

notes: Ролик с плашками на игре Dandiya Beat (чистая игра вышла 27.10): привычное колесо удачи на сайте против игры, где скидку решает точность.
С 27.10 ролики с плашками выходят и в LinkedIn: этот — первый по новому правилу.

linkedin.text:
A spin-to-win wheel gives every shopper a random code. Nobody earns it, and nothing brings them back.

Here is the same popup slot with a rhythm game instead.

The store in the video is a demo. The game is a 45-second round for Navratri: mirrors fall in time with the music, and you strike as each one meets the line.

How the pieces work for CRM:

1. The tiers are on the first screen: 10% for anyone who finishes, 15% from 60% accuracy, 20% from 85%.
2. Nobody loses. Finish the round and you still get a code.
3. While you play, a bar shows "On track for 20% off". That keeps people going to the end.
4. One round per night, nine nights in a row. That's a reason to come back tomorrow.

A wheel takes one click. This takes 45 seconds, and the shopper leaves with a score to beat, not only a code.

One catch: a rhythm game works best with sound on, and plenty of people shop with their phone muted.

You can build your own with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

Would your customers play for 45 seconds, or do they just want the code?

items.shortsTitle: Points, not a discount: a Bonfire Night game where every reward needs an order
items.hook: A Bonfire Night fireworks game that pays out bonus points instead of a discount.
items.body: Every round wins points, a better score wins more, and each reward comes with an order threshold. The points arrive with a purchase, so the shop pays only when someone buys.

linkedin.text:
Most holiday promos end up as a discount. 20% off, and customers learn to wait for the next one.

For Bonfire Night I tried a different reward: points.

The game is short: 40 seconds of fireworks in the shop of a made-up brand. Tap the rockets, don't break the streak, and the score picks the reward:

↳ a high score gets 500 bonus points
↳ a good one gets 250
↳ any finished round gets 100

One rule makes it work: points come only with an order over a set amount, and the top reward asks for the biggest basket. The shop gives points only when someone actually buys. The reward card even suggests an add-on to get a smaller basket over the line.

Why points and not % off? A discount is gone at checkout. Points stay in the account and bring people back for the next order.

To be fair, this only works if your loyalty program is worth coming back to. If nobody knows what 500 points buy, it's just a number on a screen.

You can build a game like this with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

Points or a discount: which one would your customers pick?

items.shortsTitle: Type an email, get the code, leave the marketing box unticked
items.hook: A popup game for list growth: one email unlocks 15% off, and the marketing box stays unticked.
items.body: Consent is its own choice, so your newsletter goes only to people who ticked the box. The code itself needs just the email.

linkedin.text:
Some signup popups pre-tick the newsletter box and hope nobody looks. Under GDPR, a pre-ticked box is not valid consent.

This one asks for less.

The shop here is invented: a coffee brand with a Halloween game in a popup. You decorate a pumpkin with stickers and tap Done.

How it handles the email:

1. Everyone who finishes gets the same reward: 15% off. No score to beat.
2. The code stays blurred until you enter an email. One field, one button.
3. The marketing box sits under the field and stays unticked. The code unlocks without it.
4. Only people who tick the box go to your newsletter. Everyone else still gets their code.
5. The code works at checkout, so the first order comes with the discount.

A typical popup trades 10% off for an email and a newsletter in one move. Here the shopper makes two separate choices.

The catch: the list grows slower, because fewer people tick the box. And 15% for every player is a fixed cost, so check it against your margin.

You can build your own with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

Fewer subscribers who chose to be there, or more who never saw the box: which list would you rather have?

expertPost.title: Post #97 - Links Libruary 2 - 6 GAMIFICATION READS OF 2026 THAT WILL SURPRISE YOU
expertPost.text:
I've created 100+ gamification projects for brands. And yet, every month I come across a case that makes me think, "Wow, you could do it that way, too?"

Here are 6 recent pieces that impressed me:

Research Studies

1. Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services, June 2026
500 online grocery shoppers in the UK were randomly divided into two groups: one received a standard loyalty program, the other a gamified one.

+ People engaged more often with the gamified program and became more attached to the store.
+ Personal progress worked better than competing with others.

Read: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jretconser.2026.104834

2. hello again: Loyalty Report for Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, 2026
2,040 shoppers were surveyed.

+ 43% are willing to use game features in a loyalty app.
+ This topic wasn't in the 2023 report at all.

Read: https://www.helloagain.com/en/blog/dach-loyalty-report-2023-vs-2026-how-customer-loyalty-has-evolved

Case Studies

1. Duolingo, Q2 2026 shareholder letter

+ A one-time event let people restore a lost streak: 15.4 million did. Nearly 8 million of them had no active streak when the event started.
+ Daily active users grew 23% year over year, to 58.7 million.

Read: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001562088/000162828026053299/q2fy26duolingo6-30x26share.htm

2. Taco Bell, "Bid on Luxe," Fall 2026

+ A new mini-game in the loyalty app every week. Players earn "Paddles" for playing and use them to bid on prizes.
+ Extra Paddles for signing up for SMS: the game grows the SMS list at the same time.
+ No results are available yet, but the mechanics are worth a closer look.

Read: https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/taco-bell-adds-another-gamification-element-to-its-rewards-program

Guides

1. Insider One: When Gamification Helps and When It Hurts

+ Reward results, not clicks. If you pay for every action, people do it only for the reward and quit once it runs out.
+ The same game gets boring quickly. It needs regular updates.

Read: https://insiderone.com/gamification-customer-engagement

2. Yu-kai Chou: 90+ Statistics and Case Studies on Gamification

+ Lots of statistics in one place. A handy starting point, but verify the original sources yourself.

Read: https://yukaichou.com/gamification-examples/gamification-stats-figures/

TL;DR: personal progress and a clear goal work better than competition and rewards for every click.

Follow me @Alex Andro for more.

items.shortsTitle: Every card wins, and the top prize asks for a bigger basket: a scratch card in your cart
items.hook: A scratch card that opens from the cart: every card wins, and the top prize comes with a higher minimum.
items.body: When the order falls short, the card suggests one product to cover the difference. The basket grew 57%, and the total after the discount was still 25% higher.

linkedin.text:
A discount code usually makes an order smaller. This one is set up to make it bigger.

The brand is fictional. Picture a coffee shop that puts a Christmas scratch card inside its cart.

How the card works with the basket:

1. Every card wins: 20%, 15% or 10% off. The odds are on the start screen, before anyone scratches.
2. The prize is drawn when the card is dealt. Scratching only reveals it.
3. Each prize has its own minimum order, and the top one needs the biggest basket.
4. The game knows the cart total. If the order is below the minimum, the card suggests one product that covers the difference.
5. The shopper adds it, and the code is applied at checkout.

Here the basket grew by 57%. After the 20% off, the shopper still paid 25% more than the original cart.

The catch: the add-on has to be something people want anyway, not filler. And one card in twenty gives 20% off, so run the numbers on your margin before launch.

You can build your own with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

Would you rather give everyone a small discount, or a bigger one that asks for a bigger basket?

We gave an AI one prompt and asked for a Christmas game. What came back was something you can actually play.

1. Pick where you sell and a month. The calendar only shows occasions people there really celebrate.
2. Pick the occasion and a mechanic. Mechanics are ranked by fit, and the ones that would feel wrong are filtered out, each with the reason.
3. Pick a goal. "Raise order value" adds cart thresholds and an add-on suggestion to the brief.
4. Copy the prompt and paste it into Claude Code or Codex, in an empty folder.
5. The AI writes a five-line plan, then the game: one HTML file of 939 lines, a README and a balance simulation.

The brand is made up, and the video is sped up: the real build takes minutes, not seconds.

The catch: it is a draft. Nobody has reviewed the code, the codes are placeholders, and there is no server behind it. Good for showing your team an idea before you spend budget, not for a live campaign.

linkedin.text:
Most discount popups give the same 10% to everyone who closes them. Nobody remembers that code a day later.

This one makes people work for it, a little.

The brand is invented: a luggage company with a packing game for World Tourism Day. You get one minute to fit travel gear into a suitcase, and not everything fits.

How the reward works:

1. The tighter the case, the bigger the code: 20% for a perfect pack, 15% for a good one, 10% for everyone else.
2. A meter on the side shows how close you are to the next tier while you play.
3. Every player gets a code and free shipping. A messy pack still wins something.
4. A perfect pack is possible, so skill matters more than luck.
5. The code goes on at checkout, like any other discount.

Why it can beat a flat 10%: a discount you earned feels different from one you were handed, and the game buys about a minute of attention before the shop.

The catch: 20% for the best players is a real cost, and good packers will share the trick. Check your margin, or cap the top tier.

items.shortsTitle: Release week on a merch shop: a night-drive popup game that swaps a reward for an email
items.hook: Release-week traffic comes and goes fast. Here a popup game turns one short visit into a contact and a first order.
items.body: The shop page opens a neon road game with three reward tiers: 10, 15 or 20% off. To see the code, the player types their email, while the box for news stays empty unless they tick it. Then the code is ready for checkout.

linkedin.text:
Big release weeks bring a wave of visitors to your shop. Most of them leave, and you never hear from them again.

This is a small popup game built for that moment. The merch shop is invented for the demo: it runs a neon road game during the week of the GTA 6 launch.

Here is the flow:

1. A popup on the shop page offers a 45-second drive. One tap jumps, a longer press jumps higher.
2. Before the start, the player sees the reward ladder: 20% for the finish line, 15% for most of the road, 10% for every player.
3. After the drive, a single field asks for their email to reveal the code.
4. The news checkbox stays empty. Only people who want updates tick it.
5. The code is ready for checkout, so the visit can end with a first order.

Why I like it here: the popup gives visitors something to do instead of a bare form, and the contact comes with a reason to buy before the hype fades.

The limits: without consent, that email is only good for sending the code. Your list grows only with those who opt in, so the reward has to feel worth it. Also, in this version the email stays on the visitor's device: passing it to your email platform needs a proper integration.

You can build your own with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

items.hook: Shoppers get one gift box per day until Cyber Monday, plus a streak counter and a reminder for the next morning.
items.body: Day one ends with a code, a 1-day streak and a countdown to the next box. People who opt in get a nudge the next day, and a missed day costs a freeze, not the streak.

linkedin.text:
Black Friday traffic is easy to get once. Getting the same shoppers back on Saturday is much harder.

Here is a small game built for exactly that. The coffee brand in it is invented, and so is its sale: a daily gift box for the four days from Friday to Monday.

How it pulls people back:

1. A single box per day. Three gifts get mixed up, the shopper taps one, and every pick wins 20, 15 or 10% off.
2. The result screen shows a streak and a countdown to tomorrow's box, not just a code.
3. "Remind me tomorrow" asks for an email right there, at the moment the shopper is happiest.
4. The next morning the reminder brings them back, and the start screen says "Streak: 1 day".
5. Miss one day and a freeze keeps the streak alive. Miss two and it starts again.

Why it can work: four short visits in four days keep your shop in mind during the noisiest week of the year, and the reminder list is made of people who actually played.

The catch: a streak is just a number unless it means something. In a four-day sale I would tie it to a reward, like better odds on day four. And in this draft the reminder is only an opt-in flag: sending it needs your email tool.

You can build your own with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

It's Black Friday. By Monday you'll have a list of new buyers, and the easy move is to send them another discount.

Here is the 60-day plan instead, as a 35-second animation:

items.shortsTitle: A personal link, a Christmas mug and a 72-hour code: a win-back game for customers who went quiet
items.hook: Lapsed customers get a personal link: the game says welcome back, unwraps a market mug and hands over a code.
items.body: The code lasts 72 hours and is already applied when they open the shop. Collecting all six mugs on later visits takes it to 20%.

linkedin.text:
Win-back emails usually say the same thing: we miss you, here is 10% off. Most people delete them without opening.

This one sends a game instead. Picture a fictional shop with a Christmas market mug collection.

How it works:

1. The email carries a personal link. When the customer opens it, the game says "Welcome back" instead of a generic hello.
2. They unwrap a parcel at a market stall and get one of six collectible mugs. The first mug already gives 10% off.
3. That code lasts 72 hours, with a live countdown on the screen.
4. "Use it now" opens the shop with the code already applied, so there is nothing to copy or forget.
5. Each later visit unwraps another mug: three different mugs give 15%, the full set 20%.

What a plain discount email lacks: the customer does something before they get the code, and the short deadline turns "someday" into "this week".

The catch: this is a draft. The personal token isn't checked, every code is a placeholder, and a real launch needs your shop to issue single-use codes. Also, 15% for three mugs turned out too easy in our simulation: almost 9 in 10 players got there.

You can build your own with AI, free. The almanac is in my Featured section.

What do your win-back emails offer right now: a discount, or something to do?

items.shortsTitle: Black Friday buyer vs Christmas buyer: same checkout, different reward
items.hook: Black Friday buyers and Christmas buyers check out on the same page. They need different rewards.
items.body: The Deal Hunter waited all year for the price and buys for themselves. The Gift Giver buys for several people and cares about on-time delivery and easy returns. Reward the hunter with a personal category discount, a short-deadline code for order #2 and points for full-price orders. Reward the giver with service perks, points valid until next December and gift-date reminders.
items.cta: The full breakdown: Alex Andro's post on LinkedIn

linkedin.text:
Black Friday buyers and Christmas buyers go through the same checkout. Here's why one reward doesn't fit both, as a 37-second animation.

The Deal Hunter waited all year for the price, buys for themselves and compares shops.
The Gift Giver buys for several people, needs the gift on time and pays closer to full price for the right one.

Reward the Deal Hunter: a personal category discount, a short-deadline code for order #2, points for a full-price order.
Reward the Gift Giver: service perks instead of a discount, points valid until next December, gift-date reminders.

What to skip: the same 10% for everyone, and discounts on the gift's category.

The full cheat sheet is in my post from Monday.

general: Публикуйте в 15:00 по Лондону в указанный день.
В плане ролики. Исключения — LinkedIn: по понедельникам там выходит экспертный пост Алекса, а не ролик (ссылка на него — в карточке дня); по субботам с 5.12 — мем.
Два формата по очереди. Чистая игра: прохождение одной игры без текста на экране. С плашками: та же игра в задаче CRM, с плашками Playmar и призывом в конце.

Тест нового формата «Из промпта в игру» (чт 19.11): Альманах → чат с ИИ → готовая игра, с плашками и призывом. Выкладывайте на YouTube, Instagram, Facebook и в оба TikTok; в LinkedIn — по желанию, с полным текстом поста из карточки.
У каждой игры два ролика: сначала чистая игра, через одну публикацию — с плашками. Одна игра не выходит два раза подряд.

С 30.11 (план Кирилла и Дмитрия на 30.11–20.12): пн чистая игра, вт с плашками, ср чистая, чт с плашками, пт неигровой ролик, сб мем в LinkedIn. На одной неделе игры не повторяются: чистая и плашки одной игры выходят в разные недели. Поэтому у New Year, Christmas 2 и Movie Day Quiz версия с плашками выходит раньше чистой.

Неигровой ролик (пятница, первый — 27.11) — не прохождение игры, а, например, оживший читшит. Выкладывается на всех площадках; в LinkedIn по желанию, как остальные ролики. У такого ролика может быть свой призыв вместо общего — он уже в подписи.
Мем · LinkedIn (суббота, с 5.12) — только в LinkedIn. Мем 1 (5.12) — Change my mind из коллекции, мемы 2 и 3 (12.12 и 19.12) делает Дмитрий.

Ролики выходят на YouTube, Instagram, Facebook и в TikTok (Instagram: старый аккаунт отключён Meta 19.11, с 25.11 выкладываем с нового аккаунта @alex_playmar). LinkedIn — по желанию у всех роликов (с 19.11): выложили — нажмите «Выложено в LinkedIn», решили не выкладывать — «Решил не выкладывать» во вкладке LinkedIn. У роликов с плашками для LinkedIn готов полный текст поста.
По понедельникам видео в LinkedIn не выкладываем никогда, даже с плашками: этот день в LinkedIn отдан экспертному посту.
Каждый файл — один раз на площадку. Ролик не зашёл — не удаляйте его и не выкладывайте заново: YouTube считает это спамом, Instagram режет повторы.
Звук уже в файле. Не добавляйте музыку площадки, стикеры и эффекты.
Ролик не готов к своей дате — пропустите слот и напишите Дмитрию. Другой ролик вместо него не ставьте.
Пустой слот — ролика под этот день пока нет. Появится — он встанет в план с подписью. Не появится — день пропускаем.
Пост вышел — сразу отметьте площадку и вставьте ссылку на пост. Галочки хранятся только в этом браузере.

Ссылка в профиле на каждой площадке — бесплатный альманах https://playmar.io/almanac/ с меткой этой площадки: https://playmar.io/almanac/?utm_source=<площадка>&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=reels_wave1, где <площадка> — tiktok, instagram, facebook, youtube или linkedin (метка каждой площадки — в её карточке ниже). Метку не меняйте и не убирайте: по ней видно, сколько людей пришло в альманах с каждой площадки.

Статистику каждого поста снимаем дважды: на 7-й день (тот же день недели, что выход) и на 28-й. Скрины загружаем прямо здесь: день → площадка → блок «Статистика». Что снять сегодня — вкладка «Аналитика».

li: Понедельник — экспертный пост Алекса, не ролик. Видео в LinkedIn по понедельникам не выкладываем.
Ролик с плашками — по желанию. Если выкладываете, публикуйте полный текст из плана. Он длинный нарочно: в LinkedIn длинные подписи под видео набирают больше охвата, чем короткие.
Решили не выкладывать ролик в LinkedIn — нажмите «Решил не выкладывать» во вкладке LinkedIn: так видно, что это решение, а не пропуск.
Чистая игра — по желанию. Текста LinkedIn у неё нет: возьмите первую строку и описание из плана, без призыва и хэштегов.
«Из промпта в игру» — по желанию. Если выкладываете, берите полный текст поста из карточки, без ссылки и хэштегов.
Крючок — первая строка. Пустой строки сверху нет: над видео видно всего около 3 строк.
Ссылки в тексте нет: она режет охват на 16–36%. Ссылка на альманах — в разделе Featured профиля.
Без хэштегов. Не отмечайте людей ради охвата.
Никаких розыгрышей и «сыграй и выиграй»: LinkedIn запрещает конкурсы.
Через Metricool — только если видео остаётся чётким (1080p). Если мылит — публикуйте через планировщик самого LinkedIn с компьютера.
yt: Название — первая строка из плана, до 100 знаков.
Без посторонних хэштегов (#fyp, #viral и похожих): YouTube может за них удалить ролик.
Обложку не ставьте: обложка — первый кадр.
ig: С 25.11 выкладываем с нового аккаунта @alex_playmar: https://www.instagram.com/alex_playmar/. Старый аккаунт отключён Meta 19.11; 19–24.11 в Instagram ничего не выходило, эти кружки неактивны.
Ссылка в профиле нового аккаунта — альманах с меткой utm_source=instagram, как в общем правиле.
Подпись — как в плане. До «ещё» видно около 125 знаков, поэтому суть — в первой строке.
Без призывов «напишите слово в комментариях — пришлём…».
Музыку не добавляйте: звук уже в файле.
Автокопия на Facebook — выключена. На Facebook — отдельный пост.
fb: Публикуйте на страницу через Metricool, а не копией из Instagram.
Подпись та же, что в Instagram.
Без призывов «напишите слово в комментариях…»: Facebook считает это накруткой вовлечения.
tt: Подпись — первая строка, одно предложение, призыв и 4 хэштега.
На каждом посте включите пометку «Your brand» (раскрытие рекламы). Она обязательна с 24 сентября 2026 года, без неё TikTok режет охват. Если Metricool её не ставит — публикуйте из приложения TikTok.

general: Снимайте все экраны статистики ролика целиком, сверху донизу: обзор, удержание, аудитория. Не обрезайте: цифры читаем прямо со скрина.
Один скрин — один экран. Несколько экранов — несколько скринов, их можно выбрать разом.
Ошиблись постом или площадкой — удалите скрин здесь же и загрузите в нужный.

li: Статистику поста видит только автор: снимает владелец профиля.
Под постом — «Аналитика» (View analytics): показы, охват, просмотры видео, время просмотра, реакции, комментарии, репосты, переходы в профиль, подписки.
Отдельно — кто смотрел: должности, компании, страны, доля показов своим и чужим (in network, out of network).
yt: YouTube Studio → Контент → Shorts → ролик → Аналитика: вкладки «Обзор», «Охват», «Вовлечённость», «Аудитория».
Нужны: просмотры, вовлечённые просмотры, «показано в ленте», «смотрели или пролистали», среднее время просмотра, график удержания, страны.
ig: Нужны: просмотры, охват, подписчики и не подписчики, среднее время просмотра, лайки, комментарии, пересылки, сохранения, действия в профиле, подписки.
